title: Sore throat on carbimazole (telephone) — prioritise the dangerous decision

blocks.text: Sore throat on carbimazole (telephone) — prioritise the dangerous decision

AMaC MRCP PACES23 • Round 5 • R5-232 • Station 2: Consultation (acute presentation) • 20 minutes • Skills A–G (clinical examination as indicated) • 14 October 2026 • Unofficial educational marking descriptors

A 42-year-old taking carbimazole for Graves disease telephones with a sore throat and fever that began overnight. They ask whether to take their next dose and book a routine appointment. Take a focused history, assess immediate safety and agree the initial management with the patient or caller.

sections.heading: 4. The Hook and the Examiner Trap

blocks.text: HOOK: Possible carbimazole-induced agranulocytosis with infection; the neutrophil count cannot be inferred from symptoms.

TRAP: Do not advise taking the next carbimazole dose or waiting for routine blood monitoring. A patient who is breathless, confused, very unwell or unable to attend safely needs emergency ambulance assessment.

rows: “I need to check whether you need urgent help.”

Do not advise taking the next carbimazole dose or waiting for routine blood monitoring. A patient who is breathless, confused, very unwell or unable to attend safely needs emergency ambulance assessment.
“I’ll ask questions that distinguish the causes.”
Ask about fever, mouth ulcers, malaise, chills, severity and swallowing/breathing symptoms, onset, carbimazole dose and any previous low neutrophil count. Establish immediate access to medical care.
“There is a concern that needs checking.”
Possible carbimazole-induced agranulocytosis with infection; the neutrophil count cannot be inferred from symptoms.

Tell the patient to stop carbimazole immediately and obtain urgent same-day full blood count with differential; if fever/systemically unwell, send to emergency assessment for neutropenic sepsis pathway without waiting for results. Inform endocrinology.
Labels sore throat a routine viral illness
Treats fever or systemic illness as potentially serious infection
Tells patient to take the next dose
Advises stopping carbimazole now pending urgent clinical assessment
Explains not to restart until medically advised, and documents action
Arranges same-day clinical assessment and immediate FBC with differential
Directs emergency care if fever, rigors or deterioration and alerts receiving team
Checks fever, mouth ulcers, timing of drug, infections and other medications
Identifies signs of sepsis and unsafe travel
Excludes agranulocytosis based on mild symptoms
Explains neutrophil count is needed to diagnose agranulocytosis
Arranges urgent specialist advice about antithyroid management
Uses teach-back and clear same-day action plan
Warns about severe illness and avoids delaying antibiotics when sepsis is suspected

blocks.text: Patient says “My throat is only a little sore. Can I wait until Monday?” Give only history elicited by candidate; do not volunteer the diagnosis or investigation results.

“Before assuming that diagnosis, I should consider: An ordinary viral pharyngitis is possible, but this cannot safely be assumed while taking an antithyroid medicine.”

THINK: Possible carbimazole-induced agranulocytosis with infection; the neutrophil count cannot be inferred from symptoms. SAY: explain uncertainty clearly. DO: Tell the patient to stop carbimazole immediately and obtain urgent same-day full blood count with differential; if fever/systemically unwell, send to emergency assessment for neutropenic sepsis pathway without waiting for results. Inform endocrinology. NUMBERS: 20-minute consultation. TRAP: Do not advise taking the next carbimazole dose or waiting for routine blood monitoring. A patient who is breathless, confused, very unwell or unable to attend safely needs emergency ambulance assessment. FINISH: Hold carbimazole until urgent blood count and specialist advice. If agranulocytosis is confirmed, carbimazole must not be restarted; specialist treatment and alternative definitive hyperthyroidism management are required.
